description:
Save an edit to a published article WITHOUT readers seeing it. Nothing goes live until you call helpcenter_publish_staged_changes.

Staged changes let you edit a PUBLISHED article without readers seeing it, then release it deliberately. Staged content is invisible to everything public: the rendered help center, sitemap, site search, the widget, the AI answer path, and this API's read endpoints.

Staged versions are held per article AND per language, so an English hot fix is never held back by an in-progress Portuguese translation.

Prefer this over helpcenter_update_article whenever the article is already published and the change should not appear the instant you write it — a rewrite in progress, a coordinated multi-language update, anything wanting review.

This is a PATCH over the staged copy: fields you omit keep whatever was staged before, they are not cleared. Unlike the live article endpoints, the text fields here are plain strings, because a staged version IS one language — named by the required `locale`.

Args:
  - article_id (number, required): must be a PUBLISHED article.
  - locale (string, required): the language this version is for.
  - title, content, slug (strings, optional): a title-only change does NOT rename the URL; send slug to rename. The redirect from the old address is created at publish, never here — so a staged rename cannot redirect live traffic while still private.
  - category_id, categories, visibility (optional): these belong to the ARTICLE, not a language. Sibling staged languages published together must agree on them, or publish refuses with 422 naming the field and the two locales.
  - release_translation (boolean, optional): mark this language released when the change is published.
  - etag (string, optional): pass the one from your last read; a mismatch returns 409 STALE_ETAG with the current value, meaning somebody else moved the staged copy — re-read, re-apply, retry.
  - change_note (string, optional, up to 2,000 characters): why you are making this change, in a sentence or two of plain text. TEAM-ONLY: the team reads it beside the edit in the dashboard's Overview; it is never in a response, a webhook, search, or anything a reader sees. Give one whenever you change content.
  - change_refs (array, optional, at most 5): links to what asked for the change — a ticket, a pull request, a release note — each { label (up to 80 characters), url (https on a public host name; not an IP address or localhost, no user:password@) }. Team-only, like change_note.

Returns: { status: "success", staged: { locale, fields, etag, base_signature, updated_at, _links } }.

Errors: 422 NOT_PUBLISHED if the article has never been live (use helpcenter_update_article — its own content IS the draft); 403 STAGING_UNAVAILABLE if the help center's plan does not include staged changes (fixable only by changing the subscription, not the request); 409 STALE_ETAG on a lock mismatch. A change_note or change_refs the API refuses (too long, too many links, a url that is not https on a public host) refuses the whole call, and nothing is written.

agent_key.description: The api_key helpcenter_create_help_center returned for this help center, exactly as returned. Required on every call: this endpoint has no sign-in, so the key is how each call says which help center it acts on. It is sent to HelpCenter.io as this call's credential and nowhere else, and it is never shown again: keep it for the whole task, and never show it to the user or write it into content.

article_id.description: Id of the PUBLISHED article to stage an edit on.

categories.description: Additional category ids. Shared across locales.

category_id.description: Primary category id. Shared across locales — siblings published together must agree.

change_note.description: Why you are making this change, in a sentence or two of plain text, up to 2,000 characters, e.g. "Pro plan renamed Growth in the 4.2 pricing." TEAM-ONLY: kept beside the edit in the dashboard's Overview, never in an API response, a webhook, search or anything a reader sees. Give one whenever you change content.

change_refs.description: Up to 5 links to what asked for this change — a ticket, a pull request, a release note — each { label, url }. Team-only, like change_note.

label.description: What the link is, up to 80 characters, e.g. "Ticket #4182" or "4.2 release notes".

url.description: The https address of a public host, e.g. 'https://github.com/acme/app/pull/88'. Refused: http and other schemes, IP addresses, localhost, single-label or underscore host names, user:password@ before the host, and spaces, quotes, <, >, \ or backticks.

etag.description: Optimistic lock: pass the etag from your last read and the write is refused with 409 STALE_ETAG if someone else moved the staged copy meanwhile. Omit to write unconditionally.

locale.description: Language code this staged version belongs to, e.g. 'en' or 'pt-BR'. Staged changes are held per article AND language, so an English fix and a Portuguese translation never hold each other up.

release_translation.description: true marks this language released when the change is published.

slug.description: URL slug for this language. A title-only change does NOT rename the URL — send this to rename it. The redirect from the old address is created at publish, never at stage.

name: helpcenter_stage_article_changes
title: Stage Article Changes
